messages:
Raj Patel: Heads-up — I ran a small experiment to reduce tail latency from chat endpoints by adding 'soft burst lanes' on top of our continuous batcher. sketch below and results.

Raj Patel: problem: short spikes (100–200 short reqs) blow past KV cache benefits and force big windows. idea: keep a small per-tenant token-bucket + a short-lived high-priority lane that consumes tokens first, then falls back into normal coalescing.

Eva Morales: curious — how do you prevent starvation of normal batches when bursts are frequent? looks risky for multi-tenant fairness.

Raj Patel: good call. I added a refill penalty and a cooldown that demotes a tenant to "throttled" for 500ms if they overuse bursts. also a hard cap on concurrent burst lanes per-GPU.

Mike Chen: can you paste the config you tested? would like to simulate locally.

Raj Patel: sure:

```
burst_lanes:
  enabled: true
  lanes:
    - name: short
      tokens: 80
      refill_rate: 20/s
      cooldown_ms: 500
      max_concurrency: 4
    - name: long
      tokens: 250
      refill_rate: 2/s
      cooldown_ms: 2000
      max_concurrency: 1
fallback_policy: demote_to_coalesce
priority_boost_ms: 30
```

Raj Patel: result: p99 improved ~120ms for chat workloads that send many short prompts; cost: small increase in p50 (~5–10ms) for other tenants during sustained bursts.

Ana Soto: did you measure KV cache hit-rate change? bursts could reduce shared cache reuse.

Raj Patel: yes — tiny dip (~1.5%) in KV hit-rate on heavily shared GPUs during the burst windows. I think that's acceptable vs p99 improvements for customer-facing latencies.

Eva Morales: operational concerns: how do we expose knobs? we should avoid too many per-tenant flags. maybe have a tiered default: free/standard/premium profiles with different bucket sizes.

Mike Chen: agree on profiles. Also add telemetry: per-tenant burst_count, demotions, burst_duration, and per-GPU burst_concurrency. plus an alert if demotions spike > 5% in 5m.

SRE-bot: deploy-check: ok to stage? (simulated load) :eyes:

Raj Patel: staging rollout next week, will run 48h A/B with control group. tagging @eva for fairness checks and @ana for cache regressions.

Eva Morales: thanks — will craft fairness matrix. quick note: ensure demo tenants can't game refill (we need anti-abuse heuristics, e.g., minimum inter-burst gap).

Ana Soto: I'll add KV cache time-window breakdowns to the eval dashboards.

Mike Chen: one more ask — add a graceful degrade path: if burst lanes saturate, prefer shedding low-priority microrequests rather than letting normal batches stall.

Raj Patel: yep added "shed_low_priority_on_saturation" flag in the experiment. will post results after A/B completes.

SRE-bot: scheduled rollout: eng-runtime/stage -> 2026-03-22T03:00:00Z (dry-run).
